title: Vita et passio S. Caecilii Cypriani
author: Pontius Diaconus
source: Translated by Claude from stoa0233d.stoa001.opp-lat1, as held by Open Greek and Latin's CSEL.

passages.original: Sic consummata passione perfectum est, ut Cyprianus qui bonorum omnium fuerat exemplum etiam sacerdotales coronas in Africa primus imbueret, quia et talis esse post apostolos prior coeperat. ex quo enim Carthagini episcopatus ordo numeratur, numquam aliquis quamuis ex bonis et sacerdotibus ad passionem uenisse memoratur.
passages.english: So, when his passion had been completed, it was brought to pass that Cyprian, who had been an example of all good things, was also the first in Africa to stain the crowns of bishops [with blood], because he had also been the first after the apostles to begin to be such [a man]. For from the time when the succession of the episcopate at Carthage has been counted, no one, even among good men and bishops, is recorded ever to have come to martyrdom.
passages.notes: "imbueret" (literally "imbue, dye, initiate") is taken as "stain/consecrate [with blood]", in the sense of being the first to begin the bishops' crowns of martyrdom. "sacerdotales" and "sacerdotibus" refer to bishops, as is usual in Cyprianic usage. "quamuis ex bonis et sacerdotibus" is rendered loosely as "even among good men and bishops".
